headline: Lifetime income streams offer significant age pension assets and income test advantages, making early investment more beneficial
reasoning: Justine Marquet explains that lifetime income streams are assessed at only 60% of the original purchase amount under the assets test, compared to full value for account-based pensions, term deposits, shares, and managed funds — a 40% reduction. Critically, this assessed amount is based on the original purchase price and does not grow with actual investment earnings over time, meaning earlier investment locks in a more favourable base. On the income test side, only 60% of income received from lifetime income streams is assessed, providing a 40% discount, and these income streams are excluded from deeming altogether.
quote: What happens is only 60% of the purchase amount is is tested for the assets test, rather than the whole amount of the investment, which would occur with other types of financial investments, like most other assets in your account based pension or term deposits or shares or managed fund values. So that's a 40% reduction in the assets test, and that is based off the original purchase amount. And that's deemed over time. But it doesn't grow over time with the actual earnings of the investment. So you can you can get a distinct advantage by investing earlier. And then on the income side, income from lifetime income streams, uh, only only 60% of the income is assessed. So you're getting a 40% discount on the assessment under the income test. Um, that's of the actual income received. Uh, not of any deemed amount. So they're excluded from deeming altogether.
episode_title: Why a bigger pension may not mean more income | the advisory

headline: Allianz Retire+ warns rising deeming rates may partially offset age pension increases for retirees
reasoning: While the age pension is increasing (singles ~$37/fortnight, couples ~$55.60/fortnight combined), deeming rates are also rising by approximately 50 basis points to 1.75% (below $66,800 for singles / $110,600 for couples) and 3.75% above those thresholds. This means Centrelink will assume higher income from financial assets, potentially reducing part-pension entitlements even if actual investment income is unchanged. The net benefit of the pension increase could be partially offset for part-pensioners and those with higher investment balances. Marquet emphasises that retirement outcomes depend on the interaction between investment strategy, drawdown strategy, and means-testing rules — not just investment performance alone.
quote: I don't think it tells the whole story, uh, because at the same time that the age pension rates are increasing, uh, thresholds are increasing. That means testing thresholds, but also deeming rates are increasing. So Centrelink will be assuming a higher income is being earned from financial assets... you know, the potential impact of that, particularly for part, pensioners or people with higher investment levels, is that it could partially offset any benefit from the higher age pension rates.

headline: Allianz Retire+ highlights structural benefits of lifetime income streams in reducing means-tested asset and income assessments
reasoning: Lifetime income streams are not assessed as standard financial investments under Centrelink means testing; they attract a discounted assets and income test, which can meaningfully improve a retiree's age pension entitlements. The benefit is amplified the earlier a retiree invests in such products — investing pre-retirement can generate enhanced outcomes by the time retirement commences. Two retirees with identical asset levels can achieve very different retirement income outcomes purely based on how their assets are structured. This creates a significant advisory opportunity for retirees near means-test thresholds.
quote: By including a lifetime income stream as part of your retirement portfolio, uh, it can have really different outcomes because it's just not deemed as a financial investment. It has a different assets in factored. A discounted assets and income test will apply to to money that you're receiving and assets that you have in lifetime income streams that you have invested in them and and the value of those and the impact that it has on, say, age, pension and your overall retirement income can be magnified the earlier that you decide to invest in these kinds of, of products and structures. So by investing pre-retirement, you get enhanced outcomes by the time you get to retirement just because of the way the rules work.

headline: Age pension thresholds rising creates opportunity for part-pensioners to review retirement income structures
reasoning: Justine Marquet highlights that rising age pension thresholds mean some retirees who previously didn't qualify may now be eligible for part pension entitlements. The age pension is indexed regularly and can serve as supplementary income, particularly for younger retirees or those who have drawn down significantly on their portfolios. Access to the pension can also unlock the Pensioner Concession Card or Commonwealth Seniors Health Care Card, plus new government taxation arrangements may provide additional advantages when disposing of larger assets.
quote: I think it's a real opportunity to start looking at your structures and, and revise your retirement income plan if you're a part pensioner and if you, um, are quite close to those thresholds, which, as I mentioned, are also increasing slightly. So, um, you may be able to get some entitlement where you otherwise didn't think that you could. And of course, this is you know, the age pension is supplementary income that's also indexed on a regular basis. So that can be hugely helpful to someone to supplement their savings. Particularly younger retirees that haven't been able to accumulate so much, or people who've already drawn down quite a bit in their retirement portfolio.
